https://jeffries.house.gov/2026/11/27/sp: November 27th, 2026 | Press Release SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES STATEMENT ON THE PASSING OF SENATOR ANDREA STEWART-COUSINS Today, Speaker-Designate Hakeem Jeffries released the following statement: I am incredibly saddened to learn of the passing of my good friend, the indomitable Senator Andrea Stewart-Cousins. She broke barriers as the first woman to lead a conference in the New York State Legislature, the first woman to serve as Senate Majority Leader and the longest-serving Democratic Majority Leader in New York State history. A generation of leaders have benefited from her counsel, wisdom and guidance. We came into the Legislature together and it was a blessing to watch her historic and trailblazing rise. While leading the Senate, Andrea brought stability back to the state government and oversaw the passage of major budget bills that uplifted the least, the lost and the left-behind. She championed legislation to reform the criminal justice system, protect women’s healthcare and strengthen our state’s education system. New York State is a better place today thanks to her distinguished service. My prayers and condolences are with Andrea’s children, grandchildren and all who knew and loved her. May Leader Stewart-Cousins forever rest in power. ### Back to News Share: Facebook Twitter
https://jeffries.house.gov/2026/11/25/sp: November 25th, 2026 | Press Release SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES ON MEIDAS TOUCH: “WE’VE PROMISED TO DELIVER AFFORDABILITY AND ACCOUNTABILITY. WE’RE GOING TO KEEP THOSE PROMISES” Today, House Speaker-Designate Hakeem Jeffries appeared on Meidas Touch, where he discussed House Democrats’ commitment to spend the first 100 days of the new Congress passing legislation to make life better for the American people by lowering the high cost of living and holding the crooks in the Trump administration accountable. BEN MEISELAS: Now I want to bring on Speaker-Designate Hakeem Jeffries. Speaker-Designate Jeffries, great to see you. I want to get right into it and talk about the first 100-day agenda that Democrats in the House will pursue. And I just want to confirm that these are the types of bills that we will see in 100 days, and so we can get into it, but I know our audience really just wants to hear, kind of, yes or no. Is this something that the Democrats in the House are going to pass in 100 days? Let’s just get right into it. One, pass the PRO Act and protect the right to organize. SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Absolutely. In fact, our commitment is to making sure that organized labor can not just survive in this climate, but thrive . Because the men and women of organized labor have been the bedrock of building the American Dream in this great country. BEN MEISELAS: All right, number two, end Citizens United and deal with all of these PACs that are putting all this money into politics. End Citizens United—will we see a bill in the first 100 days? Yes or no? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Well, that’s my commitment, absolutely. We need to get big money out of politics, and our plan is to bring a constitutional amendment to end Citizens United . BEN MEISELAS: Provide universal healthcare. This is critical. I’ve heard you talk about it. Provide universal healthcare. Will we see a bill that looks like that? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Well, our commitment is to make sure that healthcare is affordable for every single American. And it’s our view that we’ve got to do two things initially. We have to reverse the Medicaid cuts that are going to be devastating and will take effect in the first six months , unless we act and act decisively. And we know, because of the One Big Ugly Bill, it’s the largest cut to Medicaid in American history, approximately a trillion dollars. And people are going to get hit hard all across America. And then we also have to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits so that we can protect the healthcare of tens of millions of Americans who currently are experiencing premium increases, in some cases, of over $1,000 a month. But we know, Ben, that we can’t simply repair the damage that has been done, because the status quo that existed before the Trump extreme policies were not acceptable. And so, our view is that we have to march toward universal access to healthcare for every single American. And the steps that we can take in that regard include lowering the age of eligibility for Medicare, expanding Medicare coverage to include vision, hearing and dental and making sure that we cover every single child in the United States of America. BEN MEISELAS: You know, I’ve seen your plan that you’ve talked about looks a lot like Senator Bernie Sanders’ plan. It’s a lot [like] what Senator-elect Dr. Abdul El-Sayed has been saying. I just want—you’ve heard them talk about your plan. You’ve talked to them, I believe, about the plan. Are these—are we talking about the same thing here? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: We’re talking about the same thing and the same approach without question, and it unites Democrats , I think, across the ideological spectrum in the House and in the Senate. And one of the things I’ve talked about moving forward in terms of how we actually get it done is that we have four committees of jurisdiction that are going to be relevant here. In the House, we have Frank Pallone and the Energy and Commerce Committee. We also have Richie Neal and the Ways and Means Committee. Those two committees have jurisdiction over the issue of healthcare in the United States of America. And then in the Senate, we have Ron Wyden and the Senate Finance Committee, along with soon-to-be Chairman Bernie Sanders, the OG from Brooklyn, who’s going to be chairing the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee with direct jurisdiction over healthcare. And so, it’s my expectation that the Members on those committees, those Chairs, are going to work together to actually achieve this type of dramatic progress that we need to deliver for the American people . BEN MEISELAS: Right, and so when our audience was watching the Bernie Sanders Fight the Oligarchy Tour, and they were seeing the plan that he was talking about in 2025, I just want them to know that’s the plan that we’re basically talking about—the committee chairs are working together. We’ll keep going down this list right over here. Banning gerrymandering. Obviously, we’ve seen Democrats push for this. Republicans always try to block it. It kind of backfired in their face, but ban gerrymandering. Will there be a bill that looks like that? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Well, certainly, within the first year, we want to move legislation that prohibits partisan gerrymandering and also prohibits mid-decade gerrymandering . But at the same period of time, I want to be clear, we’re not going to unilaterally disarm. Now, we just crushed the Republican gerrymandering scheme. Every single Democrat who ran for reelection in a gerrymandered district designed to defeat them won. We didn’t lose a single incumbent. And we flipped seats in many of the states that Republicans gerrymandered to try to artificially hold on to their majority. That, of course, happened in Texas, where we flipped several seats. It happened in North Carolina, where we’re on track, if you can believe it or not, Ben, to flip seven seats. It happened in Tennessee, of course, where we flipped the seat in a gerrymandered state, and then we held on to seats in other parts of the country. And then flipped seats, of course, in California and in Utah. So we’re not going to unilaterally disarm if Republicans continue to try to engage in aggressive mid-decade gerrymandering . At the same period of time, we believe that the right approach is to ensure that it’s the American people who have the opportunity to decide who will represent them in Congress, not Donald Trump and MAGA extremists. So we are going to aggressively move legislation to end this practice. BEN MEISELAS: Ban congressional stock trading. That’s got to go. It’s got to go. It’s ridiculous. It’s ridiculous. SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Yeah, very early on, and I’ve been very clear on this throughout, that we got to clean up the mess in Washington, D.C. , but cleaning up the mess does start at home. And so, while we got to deal with the Supreme Court, and we will, and while we have to deal with the Trump administration, and we will, we’re going to move an aggressive bill early in the new Congress to ban Members of Congress from trading stock . BEN MEISELAS: And the White House, right? I mean, stop the Trump White House, I mean all the ridiculous stuff that’s going on there. Ban White House, ban Congress stock trading. Will that be lumped together, different bills, or how do you see that? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Yeah, well, we’re in conversation with some of the leaders of that effort, and that includes Seth Magaziner and Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, both of whom have done a great job, along with Pramila and others, Joe Morelle, who’ve been working on this. But I believe, certainly, that we need to end the practice across the federal government . So we need to end it in Congress. We certainly need to end it with respect to the Supreme Court and impose ethical rules of conduct on the Supreme Court since they refuse to impose it on themselves, which is crazy. And then, of course, we definitively have to deal with the President, the Vice President and the Cabinet Secretaries. BEN MEISELAS: I heard you say enact major Supreme Court reform, or words to that effect. This Supreme Court right now is so out of touch with where the American people are. Look, there’s been a lot of bipartisan bills historically. I mean, you go back to the great compromises, reach civil rights, voting rights, on and on and on, elections, you know, election integrity, all of these things. You know, McCain-Feingold, the stuff post-Great Recession, Dodd-Frank, I mean, and these are compromises, these are bipartisan bills. And the Supreme Court said, ‘You know what, based on what we’ve divined and the oracles have told us on top of the hilltop, we think the Constitution says that these people can’t come together.’ So I know our audience wants to see major Supreme Court reform. Talk about that. SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Well, certainly, this is an effort where I expect soon-to-be Chairman Jamie Raskin and Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee to spend a lot of time, energy and focus. And I’ve talked to Jamie about this and indicated that I’m all for dramatic Supreme Court reform so we can rein in an out-of-control right-wing group of extremists who have now gutted the Voting Rights Act and gutted reproductive freedom for tens of millions of women all across the country. Both those decisions are inconsistent with where the will of the American people is at. And it’s not even a close question. And so, we definitively need to deal with this question. It’s something that will be, I think, at the top of the agenda, which is going to be a very busy agenda for the House Judiciary Committee Democrats. BEN MEISELAS: Just so you know, at the end of what we’re doing, I’m having my team make a list of these things, then you and I are going to go through the list that we’re making right now, because, look, we want Congress that works. I mean, you put together a great group of candidates who won, and now we don’t just want to win for the sake of winning. We don’t want to go back to the status quo. So I’m putting up a list at the end of this, and we’re going to go through it one more time. But I want to keep going through. Raise the federal minimum wage. Has to be done. Right now, there needs to be a wage with dignity. Talk to us. Do we expect to see a bill raising the minimum wage to a wage with dignity in the first 100 days, Speaker-Designate? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Definitively, it’s my hope in the first 100 days, certainly in the first year. But we need to raise the federal minimum wage . Think about that. The fact that the minimum wage right now hasn’t been raised in 20 years and is currently, for more than a dozen states, $7.25 per hour, and that’s the federal level. That’s crazy. And we have this affordability crisis, and we have promised to do everything that we can to lower the high cost of living in the United States of America and make this country more affordable . Part of that, of course, is to lower costs in all the ways possible. So that’s housing, that’s healthcare, that’s gas, that’s goods, that groceries, that’s utilities and that’s caregiving. At the same period of time, we’ve got to raise the take-home pay of the American people . That’s also one of the reasons why we support and will continue to stand behind organized labor and protecting the right to organize, because we know that perhaps the best pathway toward a good-paying job with a living wage that allows you to live an affordable life is to be part of a union across this country. BEN MEISELAS: End the Iran War. This catastrophic war needs to end. Overwhelmingly, the American people said this war should never have been started. Will you put forward all efforts to end this war—legislation, resolutions, whatever it takes? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: In my view, we’ve got to move aggressively to end the reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, not simply in the first 100 days, but during the first 100 hours . BEN MEISELAS: Let me ask you this because Trump gave an interview with the New York Post where he’s shown—he’s choreographing what the plan is right now, right? He’s saying, ‘We won. It’s a win. The Democrats are not going to fund it, and they’re going to turn it into a loss.’ He lost the war. We know he lost the war, but this is what he always does. So he’s setting it up like, ‘We were winning, and then the Democrats didn’t fund it, so now we lost.’ And then he’s going to spend all of the next two years blaming you for everything. ‘This is why we lost the war. This is why the economy’s—’ How do you plan to deal with that? Because you know that—I read the article. It’s obvious what he’s doing. So what do you do when he does that? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Mr. President, nobody’s buying that narrative, bro. The whole situation over the last two years has been a complete and total disaster. And that’s the reason why the American people have decisively decided to move the country in a different direction. Democrats have won up and down the ballot and all across the country, and we’ve promised to deliver affordability and accountability. And we’re going to keep those promises to the American people . We know that the American people are demanding change that is bold, dramatic and meaningful, and that’s what House Democrats are going to work hard to deliver. BEN MEISELAS: Repeal the Trump Tariffs. They are announcing more of these today. This morning, they said more tariffs. It’s been catastrophic, inflation’s surging. We got the inflation report today, up 3.8%, and now they’re saying more tariffs against the world. So, repeal the tariffs? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Absolutely. The Trump Tariffs have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year. It’s one of the reasons why costs in the United States of America haven’t gone down on day one or over the last two years, notwithstanding the promises that the MAGA extremists have made, costs have gone up. You can point to several reasons for that. Certainly, the Trump Tariffs have exploded costs, and the reckless and costly war of choice has increased gas prices, food prices and fertilizer prices , which has an impact on Americans all across the country, particularly, in some cases, in farm country and on rural America. BEN MEISELAS: I’ve already heard you say earlier, reverse the Medicaid cuts, reverse the SNAP cuts, restore the ACA tax credits, all of those things part of the first-year agenda, right? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Part of the first 100 day agenda, as we’ve promised. We’ve got to move aggressively to reverse the Medicaid cuts, end the Trump Tariffs , in my view, work on that issue during the first 100 days and certainly to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits. BEN MEISELAS: Pass the Dream and Promise Act, fix this immigration system. We can have strong borders, but we got to treat people with dignity. We can’t be ripping families apart like that. Have you committed to that in the first 100 days? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Absolutely. In fact, in my view, what we need to do is that we should move the Dream and Promise Act in this Congress . We’re one Republican short of being able to do that in the House of Representatives. So we’re going to continue to work on that effort over the next few weeks. If we’re unsuccessful because we can’t find an additional Republican to actually do the right thing and protect DACA recipients and TPS recipients who are in this country, living lawfully, contributing to their communities, we certainly are committed to moving the Dream and Promise Act in the first 100 days. We have a broken immigration system, and what we have to do is fix it in a comprehensive way, in a bipartisan way , starting, in my view, as a floor, with the Dream and Promise Act. ICE is out of control, and as we’ve done throughout the year, House Democrats are not going to give a dime to the Trump administration’s violent mass deportation machine , because we do believe that we need both a safe, secure and a strong border, coupled with immigration enforcement that is fair, just and humane. That’s not what has happened over the last two years. Taxpayer dollars should be used to make life more affordable for the American people, not brutalize or kill law-abiding immigrant communities or families or individuals, and brutalize or kill American citizens, like we saw in Minneapolis with Alex Pretti and Renée Nicole Good. BEN MEISELAS: Look, I want to see—personally, I want to see ICE abolished. At the very least, though, what you’re saying is no more funding of ICE right now and claw back the money that was given—talk to us about that. SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Yeah, that’s an important point because we have to do two things. You have the regular appropriations process, and Democrats, in both the House and the Senate, we’ve been in lockstep on this issue, have refused, through the appropriations process, to give a dime to the Trump administration’s violent mass deportation machine . That will continue to be our position. At the same period of time, we have to claw back the funding that, in our view, was misappropriated to an ICE slush fund , for instance, the $75 billion ICE slush fund in the One Big Ugly Bill as part of the extreme policies that Donald Trump and the Republicans were jamming down the throats of the American people. That’s funding that actually should be used to lift up the health, the safety and the economic well-being of the American people as opposed to fueling the brutalization and killing, in some instances, of American citizens or violently targeting law-abiding immigrant communities all across the country. So we’re certainly committed to that effort. And by the way, that’s the case with respect to other aspects of the One Big Ugly Bill because, as you recall, in addition to the ICE slush fund, that bill contained the largest cut to Medicaid in American history—that’s where it all began—and also contained a $186 billion cut to SNAP, the largest cut to SNAP in American history. These extremists literally ripped food out of the mouths of hungry children, seniors and veterans . And all of this was done so they could provide massive tax breaks to their billionaire donors. We have to unravel all of that. BEN MEISELAS: So Speaker-Designate Jeffries, I had my team make a list of everything we discussed. So I just want to go down this list with yes or nos. I wrote down everything that we just said about the first 100 day to one year agenda. This way we can look back, do the interview a year from now and see what was it that the House Democrats accomplished after this landmark election. So I want to just go through it one by one, very quickly, okay? Number one, we talked about pass the PRO Act and protect the right to organize. Yes? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Of course, absolutely. BEN MEISELAS: End Citizens United, right? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Definitively. BEN MEISELAS: Provide universal healthcare and push forward legislation to achieve that, right? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: We’re going to work on that, as I outlined. BEN MEISELAS: Ban gerrymandering, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Definitively. BEN MEISELAS: Ban congressional stock trading, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Yes, very early on. BEN MEISELAS: Raise the federal minimum wage, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Absolutely. BEN MEISELAS: End the Iran War, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Very aggressively. BEN MEISELAS: Repeal the Trump Tariffs, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: They got to go. BEN MEISELAS: Reverse the Medicaid and SNAP cuts, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Definitively. BEN MEISELAS: Restore the ACA tax credits, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Definitely, very early on. BEN MEISELAS: Fix the immigration system and pass the Dream and Promise Act, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Definitely. We’ve got to turn the situation around in terms of our broken immigration system. BEN MEISELAS: Pass the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and end voter suppression, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Thank you for asking about that. That’s a high priority. We will absolutely move the John Robert Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act so we can end the era of voter suppression in the United States of America . BEN MEISELAS: Claw back the ICE slush fund, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Yes. BEN MEISELAS: And enact Supreme Court reform, correct? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Definitively. BEN MEISELAS: All right, when Trump says, ‘I’m Mr. Veto, I’m gonna veto all of this stuff. I’ll wear the veto hat. I do deranged AI images of myself. Veto, veto, veto. Look at me, look at me.’ What do you do? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Well, listen, we’re a separate and co-equal branch of government, and we’re going to move aggressively to deliver on the promises that we’ve made to the American people that you just comprehensively laid out, in that regard. And we’ll move on other things, of course, like restoring reproductive freedom for the women of America and move the Women’s Health Protection Act and other pieces of legislation designed to actually protect the reproductive healthcare of the American people. We are going to move legislation aggressively in the House. We’re going to move it over to the Senate. We’re going to work with our colleagues in the Senate on trying to get those bills through the Congress in its entirety and get those to the President’s desk . President Abraham Lincoln, my favorite Republican, once made the observation that, ‘Public sentiment is everything. With it, nothing can fail. Without it, Nothing can succeed.’ And at the end of the day, on all of the issues that we’ve discussed, we know we’re on the side of the American people. And we’re going to work aggressively to bring about the type of bold, meaningful and dramatic change that the American people are demanding and deserve . BEN MEISELAS: Speaker-Designate Jeffries, the Trump regime has been threatening oversight. They’ve been threatening to obstruct oversight. They’ve been having United States Attorneys and the DOJ send threatening letters to Democrats on the House Oversight Committee, on the Judiciary Committee. They’re doing the same thing in the Senate. What’s your response to all of that? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: The ghosts of Roy Cohn have invaded the Department of Justice. Our view is: get lost. Like really. These people are not going to intimidate Democrats from doing our constitutional duty to serve as a check and balance on an out-of-control executive branch . BEN MEISELAS: Howard Lutnick, RFK Jr., what’s your message to them right now? Especially, we see Lutnick apparently being perfectly fine with hundreds of thousands of these GPUs, these graphic processing units, getting their way to China, undermining our national security. RFK Jr., the most unhealthy agenda imaginable. America lost its measles status. I mean, Hegseth, you know, all—I could keep going—everybody out there. What’s your message to them right now? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: It’s a parade of horribles with respect to the Trump Cabinet , and certainly, the three individuals that you mentioned are going to be aggressively scrutinized in terms of the public policies that they have visited upon the American people in ways that, in my view, have been harmful. Like I explicitly called for the committees of jurisdiction to make sure that we look into this Nvidia situation and the role that Secretary Lutnick and the Department of Commerce have played in potentially jeopardizing the national security interests of the American people, perhaps for financial gain. BEN MEISELAS: Lots of—Stephen Miller’s hands are all over this. What’s your message to him? I’ve seen you make some statements about Miller. You know, when you’re in—if you go to the Oval Office or you’re having discussions or whatever happens over here or they come to Capitol Hill, I mean, do you even talk to the guy? What do you even do with someone like that who’s been so harmful to our country? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: I don’t expect to have any interaction with Stephen Miller at all . I’ll have a conversation with the President at the appropriate time, speak to the Vice President. There are a few Cabinet secretaries, perhaps, where there will be an opportunity to figure out can we find the common ground necessary with the other side of the aisle to get big things done for the American people. I don’t anticipate, at all, that Stephen Miller will be part of any of those conversations. BEN MEISELAS: Speaker-Designate Jeffries, thanks for going over that list with us. And I wanted everybody to—I wanted to really drill down on the specifics. So we appreciate you, and happy Thanksgiving. And let’s come back, you know, once Congress comes back into session, and we’ll see those bills in action. SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Look forward to it. Happy Thanksgiving to you, Ben, and to everyone out there. Full interview can be watched here . ### Back to News Share: Facebook Twitter

https://jeffries.house.gov/2026/11/24/sp: November 24th, 2026 | Press Release SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES ON FOX 5 NEW YORK: “WE’RE GOING TO FOCUS AGGRESSIVELY ON AFFORDABILITY AND ACCOUNTABILITY” Today, House Speaker-Designate Hakeem Jeffries appeared on Fox 5’s Good Day New York, where he discussed House Democrats’ commitment in the majority to passing legislation to lower the high cost of living, make healthcare more affordable and hold the crooks in the Trump administration accountable ROSANNA SCOTTO: This morning we’re going to talk with Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries. First of all, congratulations. The boy from Brooklyn did very well. SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Well, good morning. That means a lot coming from you, and thanks for having me on. ROSANNA SCOTTO: Speaker, congratulations. So what’s the first thing on your agenda that you really want to take care of, you know, when the new term starts? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Well, we believe that the American people have spoken loudly and clearly, and they want us to fight to make life more affordable for everyone, certainly here in New York City, across New York State and throughout the nation. One of the challenges that has increased costs for everyday Americans over the last year or so has been this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran. And so we’re going to move aggressively to end it. We know that the war has increased gas prices on the American people, increased food prices on the American people, increased fertilizer prices and diesel prices on farmers all across rural America in ways that have been economically painful. So we’ll move aggressively to end the war and then, of course, address healthcare, tariffs and many of the other public policy developments that have made life more expensive for the American people. ROSANNA SCOTTO: Speaker, are you concerned that some of the people affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America could stall some of your policy goals? As you know, some of them tried to stop you from becoming Speaker. Now, are you worried about them putting a wrench in your goals? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Well, the size and scale of our victory was so enormous, of course, in the House, but also in the Senate and across states throughout America. We’ll have a 260-seat majority, we believe, when it’s all said and done and every single vote has been counted. That’s going to be, Rosanna, the largest majority that any party has had this century. And we believe what does unite Democrats across the ideological spectrum is a shared commitment to bringing down the high cost of living in every area. ROSANNA SCOTTO: So I know you got, like, you know, an unprecedented 50 new seats in the House, but obviously you’re not worried about the Socialists in the House. SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Well, I think, you know, we have a very robust majority—let me put it like that—and we should have the ability to find consensus. I embrace and will continue to have an open-door policy as it relates to people articulating their perspective. But at the end of the day, we have to come together, find the common ground necessary in order to deliver the type of bold, dramatic and transformational change that the people of New York City, of New York State and America deserve. DAN BOWENS: One follow-up there, I mean, one area you may get pushback from some of the more liberal Members is on Medicare for All. There is this bill that has moved through, but you stopped short of supporting it. Why not at least let it go through a committee and see how it plays out? SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES: Well, what I believe right out of the gate we need to do is to reverse the Medicaid cuts that are going to hurt communities here in New York City, potentially close some of our safety net hospitals, or make things more economically challenging. And that, in fact, is going to be the case all across America, disproportionately perhaps in parts of rural America, where hospitals are at risk of closing and some already have as a result of the Medicaid cuts that were initially put into the One Big Ugly Bill about a year and a half ago. And so our view is that we have to move aggressively to reverse the Medicaid cuts very early in the next Congress and then, of course, also extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits so we can provide some economic relief to tens of millions of Americans who have experienced dramatically increased health insurance premiums. In some cases, those premiums have increased by more than $1,000 per month. That is unsustainable. And then, I think we have to move toward not simply restoring the status quo, but providing the American people with the best possible healthcare so that every single American can afford to go see a doctor when they need one. In my view, that’s going to require doing things like lowering the age of Medicare eligibility, expanding Medicare coverage to include hearing and vision and dental and also making sure that we cover every single child in America so that when someone gets sick, regardless of where you live in this country, a child has the ability to get high-quality, affordable healthcare. ROSANNA SCOTTO: I thought there might be like a Brooklyn coalition going on there, you know, you and Senator Schumer. DAN BOWENS: One thing we didn’t ask, if I just can, Congressman, one thing we haven’t talked about is President Trump, possible investigations, the I-word impeachment, which a lot of people say maybe this time around Democrats shouldn’t focus too much on that. We also have to clean up the mess, by the way, in our own House, which is why one of the first things that we’ll do in the new Congress is to move to ban Members of Congress from trading stock. ROSANNA SCOTTO: Hallelujah, hallelujah. Anyway, so much to be grateful for. Thank you so much, Speaker Jeffries. Getting used to that. We’re wishing you a happy Thanksgiving. https://jeffries.house.gov/2026/11/22/sp: November 22nd, 2026 | Press Release SPEAKER-DESIGNATE JEFFRIES ON CBS: “WE’RE COMMITTED TO BRINGING ABOUT THE TYPE OF DRAMATIC CHANGE THE AMERICAN PEOPLE ARE DEMANDING” Today, House Speaker-Designate Hakeem Jeffries appeared on CBS’s Face the Nation, where he made clear that in the 120th Congress, House Democrats will use our majority to fight to make life more affordable for the American people, to expand access to healthcare and to fix our broken immigration system. MARGARET BRENNAN: We turn now to the incoming Speaker of the House, Democratic Congressman Hakeem Jeffries who joins us from New York. Good morning, Mr. Speaker-Designate. LEADER JEFFRIES: Good morning, great to be with you. MARGARET BRENNAN: Well, you have, really, a huge role to take over in January. And I want to lay out for you what we saw in our exit polls as the message sent by voters. 89% said cost of living was crucial or a major factor in their vote. 90% said the same about corruption. Given those dual messages, what is the first bill you try to pass, and will it be bipartisan? LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re going to work incredibly hard to deliver on our promises to the American people around affordability and accountability. We have to drive down the high cost of living. Life is way too expensive. There are far too many people who are working hard. They’re playing by the rules. They can’t thrive, and they can barely survive. There are several things that we plan to do very early on in the new Congress. We need to end this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran that has skyrocketed gas prices, food prices and diesel prices. We need to reverse the Medicaid cuts. We need to restore SNAP benefits. We need to deal with the Trump Tariffs, which have also increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year. And, of course, we need to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits. MARGARET BRENNAN: But when I asked about whether or not it would be bipartisan, some of the things you’ve just laid out, it really doesn’t seem likely that the President, a Republican President, would sign off on. Some of the things you listed there were part of his signature tax and spending bill that Republicans passed. Are you going to send these as messaging vehicles? LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re committed to delivering the type of bold, dramatic and meaningful change that the American people are demanding. When we moved earlier this year to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits, that was bipartisan in the House of Representatives because the reality is tens of millions of people in this country—hardworking, working-class, middle-class folks, those who aspire to be part of the middle class— have experienced dramatically increased health insurance premiums, in some cases more than $1,000 per month. That’s unacceptable. Reversing the Medicaid cuts will help out people all across this country— MARGARET BRENNAN: You don’t think Trump will veto that— LEADER JEFFRIES: In rural America, urban America, small town America, the heartland of America and Black and brown communities all throughout America. Listen, that remains to be seen. We have three areas that we need to work on. We need to drive down the high cost of living and deal with the affordability crisis. We have a broken healthcare system. We need to fix it and then make sure that we actually don’t simply return to the status quo, but we do much better than what currently exists. And we need to fix our broken immigration system as well. And those are three possible areas to explore whether we can work together with the President and our colleagues on the other side of the aisle. MARGARET BRENNAN: There are a lot of different ways to define accountability. Rahm Emanuel, the former Congressman, Mayor and Ambassador, I know you know him well, told my CBS colleague that Democrats seeking accountability should move on ethics reform. He suggested a ban on stock trading and prediction markets, mandatory blind trust for everyone with over $1 million dollars in wealth and no foreign money when you’re in government or two years afterwards. Do you have an appetite for that kind of proposal? LEADER JEFFRIES: We have promised the American people that in addition to our affordability agenda, we know in the face of the unprecedented corruption that has been unleashed on the American people and the country over the last two years, that we need to deal with accountability. And we’ve made that clear. And no one is going to get a pass because there’s a cost to corruption that adversely impacts everyday Americans— MARGARET BRENNAN: But how do you define that? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, listen, we’ve got to clean up the mess in Washington. That means the Congress, that means the Supreme Court and that also means with respect to the administration. And we should begin by dealing with our own House, which is why very early on in the new Congress, House Democrats are going to move to ban Members of Congress from trading stocks. MARGARET BRENNAN: We will see if that gets the bipartisan support needed. I want to ask you as well about what President Trump said he thinks he can work with you on. He said, ‘We can get a lot of great things done.’ Take a listen. RECORDING OF DONALD TRUMP: I’m open to great healthcare. Now, can it be what they want? No. But it can be a combination of what we all want, and we could end up with great healthcare in our country. We could end up better than dealing with the Republicans. MARGARET BRENNAN: So what would working with him on healthcare do apart from, like you said, repealing the things that have already been passed? LEADER JEFFRIES: In addition to what I’ve talked about in terms of fixing our broken healthcare system, of course we can’t simply return to the status quo. In my view, we should lower the age of Medicare eligibility, we should expand coverage to include vision, hearing and dental and we should make sure that we cover the kids so that every single child and young American in this country can afford to go see a doctor when they need one. That’s a place where we can explore coming together. I know it has strong support among Democrats in the House and the Senate, and let’s see what’s possible in terms of what the President has said with respect to healthcare. Can you imagine how angry the American people will be with Washington if over the next two years we fail to do anything about affordability, fail to do anything about healthcare and fail to do anything about immigration? We’re committed to bringing about the type of dramatic change the American people are demanding. MARGARET BRENNAN: But you also have constraints on you, given the already over $40 trillion in debt America is carrying. You have constraints with the rise in cost of Social Security and Medicaid. How do you pay for expanding this? LEADER JEFFRIES: Those are conversations that we look forward to having as Members of Congress, both sides of the aisle, and certainly with the administration, but we have to do better. The economy is broken. Life is not working for far too many Americans, and it’s clear we can’t simply return to the status quo. This is a great country. When you work hard and play by the rules, you should be able to live an affordable life and a comfortable life and a good life. And that’s what we’re committed to bringing about for every single American in this great country of ours. MARGARET BRENNAN: So, when you were elected as Speaker-Designate, there were seven of the 11 lawmakers who voted against you who released a statement. Some of them are Democratic Socialists. And they said that they had secured commitments from you already. It was in a positive direction. Still wasn’t enough to win their vote. But can you tell us what commitments you have made to the left of your party? LEADER JEFFRIES: The only commitment that I’ve made is to continue to deliver upon the aggressive agenda that we talked about with respect to making life more affordable for the American people. And that’s in every area. We believe we have to drive down the high cost of healthcare and housing and gas and groceries and goods and utilities and caregiving. And we have plans to make sure that we aggressively engage in every single one of those areas. With respect to the House Democratic Caucus, I’m going to continue to have an open-door policy and talk to everyone. But what I believe unites us is our shared commitment to the affordability agenda and our shared commitment to making sure that if you have folks out there who’ve been stealing from the American people, screwing over the American people or shortchanging the American people, we will also hold the crooks accountable. MARGARET BRENNAN: But that doesn’t mean impeachment come January. It’s not an immediate plan. LEADER JEFFRIES: We haven’t ruled anything in, and we haven’t ruled anything out. We’re focused on actually delivering and keeping our commitment. And it’s my expectation that with respect to the accountability agenda, that everyone involved in whatever investigations are unveiled, they’re going to follow the facts, they’re going to apply the law, they’re going to be guided by the Constitution and then we’re going to let the chips fall where they may so we can deliver a government of the people, by the people and for the people that’s focused on actually making life better for everyday Americans. MARGARET BRENNAN: Speaker-Designate, we will watch your work. More questions for you, but we have to leave it there for today. But we still have Citizens United out there. And we still have the ability of these MAGA billionaires to flood into our election all of this unregulated money , not designed to help out everyday Americans or to bring about enlightened policy, but to maintain advantage and privilege for the wealthy, the well-off and the well-connected. That’s certainly something that, as House Democrats, we plan to do, and plan to do very early in the new Congress. JEN PSAKI: Listen, you’re now—you’re going to be second in line to the presidency. He’s a very popular former president, so that’s a lot of power there supporting that. It’s also, I mean, Elon Musk, obviously, just flushed $500 million down the toilet, but he’s the perfect example of this. That’s the context, it sounds like, through which it came up. And he, given his past history, there’s a lot to look into him, I think, about, or I think this is a question for you. I mean, from gutting DOGE to all of the cuts that we’re now seeing impacts of, including in our cybersecurity apparatus in the federal government. I don’t—he appeared during the DealBook Conference today. We’ve just played some of this. LEADER JEFFRIES: I think that everyone who has been part of this MAGA extremist movement that has unleashed all of this carnage and damage on the American people should be prepared to answer questions as it relates to what has happened, why it’s happened and, of course, from our view, how do we prevent this type of carnage from ever happening again. JEN PSAKI: And there’s no—my point here is there’s no attempts to rewrite his history or warm himself that is going to change who people want to investigate if they want to investigate him in Congress. LEADER JEFFRIES: Not at all. So look, we got to follow the facts. We got to apply the law. We’re going to be guided by the Constitution. We’re going to let the chips fall where they may. And we’ve promised that we’re going to deliver affordability as a priority and accountability as a priority. JEN PSAKI: Let me ask you about—you’ve laid out some of your specific priorities. I should note you’re not taking power for six weeks here, but you’ve outlined in your letter to the Caucus, when you said you were going to be running for Speaker, some of the specific things you wanted to address. You reiterated them yesterday in a press conference, including bringing down the high cost of gas and groceries, doing more about housing. Yesterday, I thought it was very interesting that you talked pretty extensively, you got quite animated talking about healthcare. Is healthcare the first step that everybody should expect come January 3? LEADER JEFFRIES: —in Iran. Well, we’ll figure out the exact order of what takes place January 3, January 4, January 5, January 6, January 7, but certainly I would say three broad areas: ending the war, stopping the Trump Tariffs and reversing the damage that’s been done as it relates to the healthcare of the American people. And that’s got to include reversing the Medicaid cuts and also extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits. I think there’s broad consensus amongst the Caucus and amongst the American people that these things need to be done. With respect to healthcare, we also promised throughout this campaign that we’re going to fight to make healthcare affordable for every single American. And that’s a two-step process. Step one is to reverse the damage that’s been done and fix our broken healthcare system in terms of what they visited upon the American people, meaning the MAGA extremists. But step two is a recognition that the status quo is not acceptable, and we’ve got to build the best possible healthcare system for the American people. And from my standpoint, yes, that absolutely should involve lowering the age of Medicare eligibility. It should involve expanding coverage to include vision and hearing and dental, and we’ve got to make sure that we’re covering every single child in the United States of America. And I believe that on the House side, led by Frank Pallone and the Energy and Commerce Committee and Richie Neal and the Ways and Means Committee, and on the Senate side, led by soon-to-be Chairman Bernie Sanders of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee and Ron Wyden, the Chair of the Finance Committee, that we can find common ground amongst our two chambers to take the type of decisive, bold action on healthcare and a whole host of other issues to basically put the American people in the best possible position so they can live an affordable life, a comfortable life and a good life. JEN PSAKI: And my bet is you all are going to pass some things, and you’re going to send it to Donald Trump and dare him to veto it. LEADER JEFFRIES: That would be correct. JEN PSAKI: Alright, House Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries. Congratulations on a huge day. Thanks for spending some time with me tonight. LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you. https://jeffries.house.gov/2026/10/21/le: October 21st, 2026 | Press Release LEADER JEFFRIES ON NEWS 12: “DRAMATIC CHANGE IS NECESSARY” House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries joined Tara Rosenblum in Brooklyn’s Shirley Chisholm State Park for a special edition of News 12’s Power & Politics, where he discussed the path to taking back the House of Representatives and how House Democrats are fighting for an affordable America. TARA ROSENBLUM: You sound extraordinarily confident that the Democrats will be able to win back the House, but we have seen here in New York where the polls have gotten a lot of big races wrong lately. So what is it that you’re seeing on the ground that makes you feel so optimistic? That’s always the best barometer, right? On the ground, talking to the voters. LEADER JEFFRIES: On the ground, I’ve been traveling the country talking to everyday Americans, and what’s clear is that dramatic change is necessary. The American people know that things aren’t going well. Too many Americans are drowning in this failed Trump-Republican economy . TARA ROSENBLUM: And we’re going to talk a lot about the economy in this interview, but first I want to drill down and go hyper-local because, as you know, a number of the tightest House races in the country are playing out right here at home. So as you’re sitting down and you’re doing this midterm math, what are the local races that you feel are the most pivotal, the best pickup opportunities towards your path to the majority? LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re working hard to make sure that Congressman Tom Suozzi and Congresswoman Laura Gillen are both reelected. They’re doing an extraordinary job on behalf of the people of Nassau County, fighting every day to try to make life more affordable . At the same period of time, in the northern New York City suburbs of Westchester and Rockland County, Cait Conley, a combat veteran, a patriot, a national security professional, is running an extraordinary race to win a seat currently held by a Republican Congressman, Mike Lawler. TARA ROSENBLUM: You have called Mike Lawler an ‘unmitigated fraud,’ yet some of your fellow Democrats have broke ranks and endorsed him, like Jared Golden. What do you make of that? And I guess the more important question is, can you flip the House if you don’t win NY-17? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, NY-17 is going to be incredibly important, and Cait is doing a great job, and I believe that she is going to be elected to Congress in November . Jared is going to have to speak for his own decisions. He’s a retiring Member of Congress. He’s from Maine, hundreds of miles away. This is a race that’s going to be decided by people on the ground. TARA ROSENBLUM: I know you’ve said that you will address this after Election Day. What do you think are the appropriate consequences for Democrats who break rank on important endorsements or critical votes? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ll have a family conversation about the best way for us to proceed in the aftermath of the November 3 midterm elections. Right now we’ve got to be all-hands-on-deck to make sure that we’re successful . TARA ROSENBLUM: You also mentioned the Long Island Congressman from our backyard, Tom Suozzi. He has made some recent statements expressing concern that the party is pouring a lot of resources into those pickup opportunities like NY-17, and perhaps short-changing safer seats like his. How do you respond to that? Is the party stretched too thin right now? LEADER JEFFRIES: Our first priority will remain making sure that our incumbents like Tom Suozzi and Laura Gillen and Josh Riley here in New York and in other parts of the country are re-elected. TARA ROSENBLUM: You know, it’s looking like a number of these tight races will come down to a few thousand votes, which means that these Independent voters will be pivotal, and when we’re out and about in the streets talking to our Independent voters, especially in the suburbs, you know, in the Hudson Valley, Long Island, New Jersey, a lot of them express just as much frustration as they feel with the President’s policies as they do with some of the leftward push from the Democratic Party. So how do you win over those Independents without alienating the progressives? And really the bigger question is, do you think that some of the Democrats’ policies have moved too far left to win the suburbs? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, what unites the House Democratic Caucus, whether that is the progressive wing or New Dems or Blue Dogs, is the fact that all of us recognize life is way too expensive . And there’s a shared aspiration to make life better for everyday Americans, working-class Americans and middle-class Americans, including those hardworking American taxpayers in the suburbs. And that really is going to be our driving, core mission, because we know that a lot of promises were made by Donald Trump and Republicans with respect to affordability, and in my view, our view, they’ve left behind a graveyard of broken promises . TARA ROSENBLUM: In addition to reversing some of Trump—President Trump’s policies, I know you’ve been an outspoken critic of his tariff decisions. Tell me a Democratic proposal that you would push for next year that would help out with affordability and help families afford food and fuel and housing costs. LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s clear to us, as Democrats, that we need to dramatically build more housing that the American people can afford . And in this Congress, we were able to pass a housing affordability bill—that is now law—that will start that process, but it’s clear that more needs to be done. So, we can enhance and strengthen the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, which is a vehicle used by affordable housing developers to build housing that working-class folks and middle-class folks and everyday Americans can actually live in with dignity and respect. We need to lean into the affordable housing space in that regard by strengthening the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, increasingly used for moderate-income housing as well. I think we need to put money in the pockets of everyday Americans by doing things like expanding the Child Tax Credit, as well as the Earned Income Tax Credit. And, of course, we also need to end this war because the war has dramatically increased gas prices, fertilizer prices and diesel costs . And that’s had an impact on the American people that is hurting their pocketbooks. TARA ROSENBLUM: And you’re referring to the Iran war? LEADER JEFFRIES: That’s correct. TARA ROSENBLUM: I know in a recent interview when you were asked about withholding funding, you stopped short. So if the Democrats take back the House, and if you become Speaker, and if President Trump continues this military option, will you pursue the House’s power of the purse to force an end to this war? LEADER JEFFRIES: I don’t want to get out ahead of the appropriators and that effort, in terms of figuring out how we deal with this issue, will be led by Rosa DeLauro, who will be the top Democrat on the Appropriations Committee and the next Chair. But we do have to look at every available legislative mean in order to do what the American people want us to do, which is bring an end to this reckless, unnecessary war . TARA ROSENBLUM: You have also said that should you—should the Democrats take back the House, you have said you will start ‘holding the crooks accountable on day one.’ And when I heard you say that, I was wondering—who is he referring to by ‘crooks,’ and what does accountability look like? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, what we’ve said is that if folks are out there, and you have been stealing from the American people, shortchanging the American people or screwing over the American people, that beginning on day one, we’re going to hold the crooks accountable. We’ve seen unprecedented corruption unleashed by the Trump Cartel, broadly defined, on the American people in ways that are inconsistent with delivering a government of the people, by the people and for the people . This executive branch, the Trump Cartel, is totally out of control. The American people know it. There’s a new scandal that arises every day. And we’ve got to clean that mess up . TARA ROSENBLUM: You have repeatedly refused to rule out impeaching the President. So looking forward, in 2028, what would it take for you to consider a third impeachment? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we haven’t ruled anything in and we haven’t ruled anything out . The oversight efforts are going to be led by the House Judiciary Committee Democrats and Jamie Raskin, the next Chair of the Judiciary Committee, who’s doing an extraordinary job, and Robert Garcia, along with the House Oversight Committee Democrats, who’s done an incredible job in trying to make sure that we are delivering transparency and accountability to the American people. They’re both professionals, and it’s my expectation that the Democrats on these two committees are going to do right by the American people. And that means following the facts, applying the law, being guided by the Constitution and then letting the chips fall where they may . TARA ROSENBLUM: Coming up, I ask Leader Jeffries who he thinks should lead the top of the Democratic ticket in 2028. Stay with us. TARA ROSENBLUM: We continue our exclusive conversation now with Hakeem Jeffries, turning our focus to foreign policy and the future of the Democratic Party. Since we’re talking about the future—I know you’re not one to hang up the curtains ahead of time. I know that’s your style—but a number of the Democratic nominees who look poised to win in November, like Darializa Avila Chevalier, have said that, well, they have not yet said that they would support you for Speaker. I know you’ve met with all of them individually as well. In those private conversations, have they indicated to you what it would take to earn their support yet? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we haven’t had that conversation, and I haven’t asked anyone for their support in connection with what may happen on January 3, which will be the date of the new Congress, because I think it’s appropriate for us to focus on getting the job done in terms of what’s in front of us, and that’s winning in what will remain a challenging environment because of the evenly divided nature of the country. TARA ROSENBLUM: Now we get to have some fun. LEADER JEFFRIES: Okay. TARA ROSENBLUM: Let’s talk 2028— LEADER JEFFRIES: All right. TARA ROSENBLUM: —and the future of the Democratic Party. I want you to name three people who you think could lead the Democratic presidential ticket. Just three. LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s a great question, but the American people are going to make that decision. I’m not going to get out ahead of the American people. I think we’ve got a lot of tremendous candidates, some Governors, some Senators, a few Members of the House who may put their hat into the ring . But until they do so, and nobody is going to declare for the 2028 presidential race until after we get through the midterm elections, I’m going to defer commenting on who hypothetically could lead. We do need a dramatic change, a next-generation Democrat to lead the party forward . TARA ROSENBLUM: Well, you mentioned next generation, and you mentioned House Members, so that made me think of Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, your fellow New Yorker. You have said that the sky’s the limit for her. Would you like to see her run for the White House, or do you think she should run for Chuck Schumer’s seat if he doesn’t run again? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, she’s going to have to make that decision on her own, which I assume she will over the next few months. TARA ROSENBLUM: Would she be a good candidate for either of those offices? LEADER JEFFRIES: She’d be a good candidate for whatever office she decides to run for. She’s an extraordinary leader who has done a great job in the House of Representatives. She’s been a great colleague. She’s led on a whole host of issues that matter to so many different New Yorkers and Americans all across the country. And it’s going to be interesting to see what decision she makes. I assume she’ll make one over the next couple of months. TARA ROSENBLUM: Do you think Chuck Schumer should run again? LEADER JEFFRIES: I think Chuck Schumer has done a tremendous job in putting the Senate into play when so many people didn’t believe that possible. And now we’re going to take back the House and are on the doorstep of taking back the Senate . And so, I’m not going to get out ahead of any decisions that Chuck Schumer may or may not make. TARA ROSENBLUM: I recently interviewed Congressman Pat Ryan from the Hudson Valley, and he sure sounded like he was interested in running for Chuck Schumer’s seat if he doesn’t run for reelection, and if AOC doesn’t run. What do you think of him as a candidate? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I haven’t talked to Pat about that, but Pat’s been a great patriot, a combat veteran, a principled next-generation leader , and I think he has a bright future. TARA ROSENBLUM: I have to get your take now on immigration and specifically the ICE shooting that just happened in our backyard in the Bronx earlier this month. Where do you think the line should be held between immigration enforcement and protecting our immigrant communities? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, ICE is completely and totally out of control. And that’s the reason why, as House Democrats, we’ve made clear that we are not providing a dime to Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine . We think that dramatic changes are necessary in order to get the situation turned around with respect to ICE, including ensuring that there are state and local independent investigations so that when the law has been broken, there can actually be accountability. We want to make sure that ICE agents are required to obtain judicial warrants before they can break into any homes, seize any individuals in manners that we believe are often inconsistent with the spirit, or the actual Fourth Amendment. We think that ICE agents should be required to wear body cameras. The masks need to come down. TARA ROSENBLUM: Ms. Chevalier was at that protest following the shooting and claimed she was thrown to the ground. And just yesterday, she called for Jessica Tisch, the NYPD Commissioner, to resign or be fired. What do you make of her comments? LEADER JEFFRIES: I certainly support Mayor Mamdani’s leadership, and support his willingness to stick behind Commissioner Jessica Tisch, who I believe has done an extraordinary job in helping to keep the City of New York safe. TARA ROSENBLUM: And of course, the divisions within your party also extend to Israel. And on October 7, you put out a statement. You said, ‘American policy in the Middle East must change dramatically.’ So what would that look like? Would you support conditioning aid to Israel going forward? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, what I support is—we have to lift up two principles at the same time. Israel’s right to exist as a Jewish and democratic state, living side by side in peace and prosperity with an independent Palestinian state, so that we can provide dignity and self-determination to the Palestinian people, which they’ve long sought but have been unable to achieve. I think America needs to reinforce its commitment to a two-state solution in order to achieve a just and lasting peace . And that, to me, is where the overwhelming majority of the American people are at. TARA ROSENBLUM: Let’s talk about now the recent rape case at Cornell, which has raised questions about how consent is defined and proven. Right now, the legal definition of consent varies state-to-state. Do you believe that there should be a uniform federal definition of sexual consent or a federal law establishing clear standards for sexual assault cases? LEADER JEFFRIES: I think we should take a look at that, and certainly as it applies to what takes place on college campuses and universities all across the country. This is a deeply searing, deeply troubling case. Serious allegations have been raised. It requires a very serious investigation. I have full faith and confidence in Attorney General Tish James and her office to professionally follow the facts and apply the law and make sure that there is justice that is brought to bear. TARA ROSENBLUM: Coming up, we go beyond politics. A more personal side of Hakeem Jeffries. That’s next. TARA ROSENBLUM : We’ve spent much of our conversation focused on the future of Congress, but to understand where Hakeem Jeffries may be heading next, we have to look back to where his story began, right here in Brooklyn. So we are sitting here in Shirley Chisholm State Park, and I know you’ve spoken a lot about the outsized influence she had on you as a young boy growing up in Brooklyn. She broke one of the biggest barriers in Congress, and now you could be on the cusp of breaking another. What do you think she would think of where you’re at right now on your journey? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, it’s an honor to stand on the shoulders—the legendary, iconic, heroic shoulders of a great leader like Shirley Chisholm , whose district I now largely represent in Brooklyn. She, of course, broke an extraordinary barrier in becoming the first African American woman ever to serve in the Congress. And she served with courage, with intellect and with boldness. And as I move forward, wherever that may lead, I look forward to continuing to channel, as best I can, her tremendous spirit of service . TARA ROSENBLUM: And I know your father passed away in 2023 before he could see you reach this point. Your mother, who grew up right in our backyard in Connecticut, also helped shape your values and commitment to public service. If you make history as the first Black Speaker of the House—I could see those words hitting you as I say them—you think that your Dad would be so proud of that moment? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ll certainly cross that bridge when we get to it in January. But it’s been a blessing to have been raised by my Mom and Dad here in Brooklyn in a union household, working-class neighborhood in Central Brooklyn, coming of age in the middle of the crack cocaine epidemic, a very difficult time, having grown up in the Cornerstone Baptist Church . And, of course, my Mom and Dad both instilling in my brother and I the value of hard work and caring for others and being community-centered. And so, as I travel along this journey, I know Dad is looking down upon my younger brother and I. And I can take comfort in that. TARA ROSENBLUM: And now you’re raising two boys of your own. As you take off the politician hat and put on the dad hat, what worries you most about the America that they’re growing up in? LEADER JEFFRIES: I think the big question that has to be resolved for the American people is: Can we keep the American Dream alive? TARA ROSENBLUM: But for now, Hakeem Jeffries’ political future rests with you, the voters, and in just a few weeks we’ll find out if his next chapter is one for the history books. I’m Tara Rosenblum. Thank you for joining us for this special edition of Power & Politics. Full interview can be watched here . Back to News Share: Facebook Twitter

But I think Ken Martin’s term is four years, and there’s no reason to believe at this point that he’s going anywhere. JOE MATHIEU: Okay, I appreciate your answering that. At the same period of time, America, the wealthiest country in the history of the world, should always have a strong floor. And we know what that looks like. That’s Social Security, that’s Medicare, that Medicaid, that’s the Affordable Care Act, that’s veterans’ benefits, that’s nutritional assistance. By the way, every single one of these things brought to you by your friendly neighborhood Democratic Party, designed to ensure that there’s a strong floor for working-class Americans, for middle-class Americans and for everyday Americans. https://jeffries.house.gov/2026/04/22/le: April 22nd, 2026 | Press Release LEADER JEFFRIES STATEMENT ON THE PASSING OF DAVID SCOTT House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries issued the following statement upon the news of the death of Congressman David Scott: Today, I join those throughout Georgia and across the country mourning the loss of a giant, Congressman David Scott. Born in the Jim Crow era, Congressman Scott went on to make history as the first African American to be Chair of the House Committee on Agriculture while fighting at every step along the way for the people he was privileged to represent. Growing up as a child on a farm in a small town in South Carolina, Congressman Scott never forgot his humble roots and always supported our nation’s farmers throughout his public service journey. David championed rural communities, ranchers and producers while making sure that families across the country have access to affordable, nutritious food. Congressman Scott helped secure $150 million in scholarships for students attending 1890 African American Land-Grant colleges and universities. In recognition of David’s incredible legacy, his beloved Agriculture Committee has advanced legislation to permanently name these grants in his honor. Throughout his decades-long tenure on the Financial Services Committee, he led numerous programs that have made a real difference in the lives of our nation’s homeowners, particularly those who struggled to keep a roof over their heads during the worst of the financial crisis. Among his many legislative accomplishments, Congressman Scott was particularly proud to fight for our nation’s veterans by ensuring that the Atlanta VA Medical Center provided the best possible care for our returning heroes. Though he will be remembered by most for his barrier-breaking Congressional service, David started an advertising agency, produced and performed in a televised special about Langston Hughes and created and hosted a national radio show focused on Black American life. Truly a trailblazing Renaissance Man, he will be deeply missed by his constituents and his colleagues in the House Democratic Caucus. Our prayers are with his loved ones during this tremendously sad time. May David Scott forever rest in power. ### Back to News Share: Facebook Twitter

https://jeffries.house.gov/2026/03/04/le: March 4th, 2026 | Press Release LEADER JEFFRIES DURING WAR POWERS RESOLUTION DEBATE: “DEMOCRATS ARE HERE TO STAND UP FOR THE RULE OF LAW AND THE UNITED STATES CONSTITUTION” Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries spoke on the House Floor in support of House Democrats’ War Powers Resolution, emphasizing that our Constitution requires the President get approval from Congress before plunging America into a war and that taxpayer dollars should be used to drop prices at home, not to drop bombs in the Middle East. President Trump has now done the exact opposite. Regime change wars are among the most expensive things that we can undertake, and yes, Secretary Hegseth, for decades, they have failed to accomplish their objective. Vietnam was a regime change war. Afghanistan was a regime change war. Iraq was a regime change war. And despite the incredible bravery of our heroes and patriots, because of failed policy decisions, they didn’t work out. Even if the Iranian regime were to fall, we have no way to control what comes next, which most experts believe would be the Iranian Revolutionary Guard-led government rising up and being just as repressive and antagonistic as the current theocracy and perhaps even more committed to the acquisition of nuclear weapons. Fifth, and most recently, Donald Trump said “I had a feeling” Iran would attack first, as some sort of rationale for going to war. Donald Trump had a feeling that Iran would attack. The United States government has initiated a war, put American lives at risk, six patriots have already been killed, thousands of American citizens are stranded in the Middle East and he has plunged the entire Middle East into a war and chaos over a feeling. Taxpayer dollars should be used to drop grocery prices, drop housing costs and drop health insurance premiums. Instead, Donald Trump is spending billions of taxpayer dollars to drop bombs in the Middle East. That has not happened, and that’s why this bipartisan resolution, led by Democrats, is on the Floor of the House of Representatives today. And as Democrats, we are committed to continuing to fight to use your taxpayer dollars to lower the high cost of living, to fix our broken healthcare system and to clean up corruption. https://jeffries.house.gov/2026/02/28/le: February 28th, 2026 | Press Release LEADER JEFFRIES ON NPR: “THE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION WOULD REQUIRE IMMEDIATE TERMINATION OF ANY ADDITIONAL MILITARY ACTION” Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on NPR’s Morning Edition, where he made clear that Donald Trump launched massive and ongoing military operations against Iran without the authorization of Congress, and Democrats remain committed to compelling a vote on a War Powers Resolution when Congress returns. EMILY KWONG: Leader Jeffries, welcome back to All Things Considered. LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you for having me on. EMILY KWONG: First, what is your reaction to reports of Ayatollah Khamenei’s death, and what does it mean for security in the region? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I’m not going to shed any tears as it relates to his death. He’s brutalized his own people and built an Iran that is the largest state sponsor of terror in the world. But what comes next is unclear because the Trump administration has not been able to articulate a plan , one, to ensure that U.S. forces are not entangled in a forever war in the Middle East, which we know would be a disaster. And this notion of regime change has never been successful, as most recently indicated by its failure in Iraq, its failure in Libya and its failure in Afghanistan. EMILY KWONG: What would a War Powers Resolution do if passed? You’ve been talking about this for a while now. Just help us understand how it could change the situation on the ground at this point. That’s, of course, consistent with what is required by the Constitution. And it’s required by Constitution because the President, on matters of war and peace, is supposed to make the case to the American people, which we believe he has failed to make at this point to justify or risk another entanglement in a failed forever foreign war. So the resolution would require immediate termination of any additional military action absent the President making his case to the American people. EMILY KWONG: How will you convince enough of your colleagues in Congress to vote for this, including those who perhaps support some kind of military action in Iran? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, it’s a bipartisan resolution that has been introduced by Congressman Khanna and Congressman Massie. We believe we will secure some additional Republican support, but we’re working on that right now. We’ll have a Caucus meeting tomorrow—on Sunday—to discuss it. We know there will be strong support for it within the House Democratic Caucus and strong opposition to what Donald Trump has done in this particular instance or moving forward. But we have a few days to be able to try to get to the 218 votes necessary to ensure that the resolution passes. EMILY KWONG: This is all happening amid weeks of negotiations with Iran. So what do you wish the Trump administration had done instead? Because as you said in a statement earlier this week, Iran should be, quote, aggressively confronted for human rights abuses, threats to allies and more. LEADER JEFFRIES: Yeah, that aggressive confrontation, in my view, should involve strong diplomacy coupled with sanctions , as were very successful under the Obama administration and being able to constrain Iran’s nuclear program. This was not an issue until Donald Trump walked away from the Iran nuclear agreement, and now has brought us to the brink of a possible war in the Middle East. EMILY KWONG: So to you, the only solution, the only way forward, is to de-escalate? Would it be responsible to walk away after the U.S. and Israel started this though? That became clear in Afghanistan and that became clear in Iraq. It will also be the case in Iran. EMILY KWONG: The U.S. and Israel appear to be working in lockstep here, and it is an alliance that is fundamentally based on security, right? February 27th, 2026 | Press Release LEADER JEFFRIES ON MS NOW: “OUR TOP FOCUS AS DEMOCRATS IS GOING TO BE TO DRIVE DOWN THE HIGH COST OF LIVING” Last night, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on MS NOW’s The 11th Hour, where he highlighted the failure of Donald Trump and Republicans to lower costs and keep their promises and reiterated Democrats’ commitments to protecting the American people. CATHERINE RAMPELL: Leader Jeffries, thank you so much for joining me this evening. LEADER JEFFRIES: Great to be with you. CATHERINE RAMPELL: So, Leader Jeffries, this was a record-breaking speech—nearly two hours as you know—and Trump dedicated less than three minutes in all of that to affordability. So many people out there said that they voted for him because of the economy, yet they are unhappy. At the same time, they aren’t exactly optimistic that Democrats can solve their issues. So how is the party going to show voters that they are able to do that? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, first of all, the best thing that I can say about the speech is that it’s over. And you’re absolutely correct. In addition to him lying throughout the entire duration of his remarks, he dedicated less than three minutes to dealing with the affordability crisis now. Donald Trump promised to lower costs on day one, and of course he’s failed. Costs haven’t gone down in the United States of America. Costs have gone up across the board on housing, on healthcare, on child care, groceries and electricity bills—all skyrocketing. Our effort will be to make clear to the American people that our top focus as Democrats is going to be to drive down the high cost of living. And we’ve seen Democrats successfully be able to make that case in places like New Jersey and New York and Virginia, as a matter of fact up and down the ballot across the country , which is the reason why Democrats have been winning elections for 14 consecutive months. And we’re going to continue to keep our foot on the gas pedal. CATHERINE RAMPELL: So I want to ask you about at least one new proposal that seems to have come out of the State of the Union address on affordability. The President mentioned a ratepayer protection pledge, which, for those watching, basically means that tech companies will build or buy their own electricity supplies for data centers. Do you support this particular idea, and if not what are Democrats’ specific plans for dealing with voters’ concerns about data centers and rising electricity costs? LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, those concerns are very real, very important.
